endpoints.description: Process is up. Never touches a dependency.
Ready to serve traffic — the database must answer.
Every monitored dependency, with latency and last error.
Branding and the OIDC coordinates the SPA needs before login.
The permission catalogue, grouped as the admin matrix renders it.
Built-in role definitions and the permissions each carries.
The API surface this process is serving.
The caller's profile, live permissions, organization and preferences.
KPIs with previous-period comparison, charts, alerts and activity.
Explorer resources, fields, operators, columns and live record counts.
Run simple and nested explorer conditions in PostgreSQL.
Headline metrics, breakdowns and a trend for the rows the current query selects.
What each dataset can be grouped by, measured by, and over which periods.
Group, measure and return — one analysis, computed in SQL.
Kanban boards this reader may open, and creating one.
One board whole — its lanes and their cards — or a change to it.
A new lane on a board, or the whole column order.
Rename a lane, change its work-in-progress limit, or remove it.
A new card on a board.
One card with its family, a change to it, or its deletion.
Put a card in a lane at a position, renumbering what it displaced.
Which datasets can be mapped, how each reaches a place, and the gazetteer.
Where one dataset is, measured one way, over one period.
Every dashboard this reader may open, or one more of their own.
One dashboard: read it, change it, or remove it.
Add a widget, and return the layout it now has.
Change what a widget asks and where it sits, or take it off.
Every widget's geometry at once, which is what one drag produces.
Every folder, what is in it, and what this reader may do.
The files in one folder, or a presigned place to put a new one.
A presigned download, a rename or a move, or a delete.
Confirm an upload — the object is checked, not taken on trust.
Create a folder.
Remove an empty folder.
Saved reports this reader may open, and creating one.
One saved report: read it, change it, or remove it.
Execute a saved report through the shared analysis compiler.
A private copy of a report, owned by the caller.
Download the current exploration as CSV, JSON or XLSX.
List visible saved searches or save the current explorer question.
Open, update or delete one visible saved search; only its owner may mutate it.
Copy any visible saved search into a new private search owned by the caller.
Transfer ownership of a saved search. Owner only, audited.
Rank one term across every dataset the caller may read.
Every dataset the caller may read, with field profiles and freshness.
One dataset's catalogue entry, or `?field=` for the values it holds.
The platform's connection map: entities, weighted relations, coverage and hub records.
A clustered slice of the record graph: nodes, edges, communities and modularity.
Everything a record points at, and everything pointing at it.
Search active colleagues, for share and assignment pickers.
Operational alerts, each linking to the records behind it.
The caller's notifications, newest first, filterable and optionally grouped, with unread counts.
Unread totals — what the header badge polls when the socket is down.
Mark one read or unread, or delete it.
Mark everything read, or everything in one category or collapsed group.
Audit filter vocabulary — fields, operators, actions and results.
The audit ledger — who did what, when, filtered and faceted in SQL.
Download the audit ledger as CSV, JSON or XLSX under the current filters.
One audit entry, with its field-level before → after diff.
The notices addressed to this reader, and writing one (announcements.manage).
Every announcement whatever its state — the author's list.
One announcement: read it, change it, or withdraw it.
Record that this reader has seen — or agreed to — this announcement.
The activity feed: what happened, filterable by kind, dataset, actor and period.
Everything recorded against one record — the detail-page timeline.
Create one entity record; the server names it.
One entity record: read it, edit it, or remove it.
What a bulk action would change, split into hand-picked and filter-matched.
Apply one change to many records; the answer carries both halves.
Two or more records side by side, with the differing fields marked.
The tag vocabulary, and adding to it.
Rename, recolour or remove one tag.
The tags on one record; PUT sets the whole set.
The signed-in reader's own page: access, work and when they work.
A colleague's page, showing only what the viewer may be told.
What is wrong with the records, counted, with somewhere to go for each.
One dataset's data-quality counts, for the indicator on its list.
The conversation on one record, and adding to it.
Change or withdraw one comment; only its author may.
The roles in force, or a new one of this installation's own.
Change what a role grants, or remove one this installation added.
People, with their role, status and sign-in history.
One person's profile and effective access, or a change to it.
Begin acting as this person; audited with both identities.
What an automation may watch and what it may do.
Every automation, or a new one.
One automation with its recent runs, a change to it, or its withdrawal.
Evaluate an automation now, as a dry run or for real.
What this automation has done, most recent first.
Everything in a window of time, expanded from its series, or a new event.
One event, a change to the whole series, or its cancellation.
Say whether you are coming.
The composer's wording, or one of them with its placeholders filled.
One action, applied to the threads somebody selected.
One folder of this reader's mailbox, newest first.
One conversation with its messages, a change to it, or its removal.
A new message: a draft, a reply, or one queued to go.
Edit a draft, send it, or discard it.
Every setting, grouped, with what the platform ships with beside it.
Change one setting, or reset it to its default.
Every feature flag and whether it is on for this reader, or a new one.
Turn a flag on or off, change its rollout, or remove it.
The log's filter vocabulary, per-level counts and retention bound.
One page of the system log, filtered and faceted in PostgreSQL.
Whatever has arrived since the caller's cursor — the live tail.
One log line in full: its context, stack trace and sibling lines.
Apply the retention policy now, as `retention.log_days` declares it.
The queue's filter vocabulary and per-status counts.
One page of the background-job queue, filtered and faceted in PostgreSQL.
One job in full: its payload, its result and its log lines.
Queue another attempt on the same job.
Stop a job that has not finished, keeping the row.
Grant a job more attempts, up to the allowed maximum.
Group kinds, the permission catalogue, and what the reader may change.
Every group, filtered and faceted — or a new one, granting nothing.
One group and its members: read, rename, or retire it.
Set who is in a group. Effective on their next request.
Set what being in a group grants. Needs roles.manage.
Tiers, statuses, regions and what the reader may change.
Every organisation, filtered and faceted in PostgreSQL.
One organisation's whole structure, or a change to its details.
Add a department, optionally inside another.
Edit or move a department, or retire it when nothing is inside.
Statuses and the scopes this caller may grant.
Every API client — or a new one, whose secret is shown once.
One client with its credentials and recent requests; edit or retire it.
Mint a new credential and put the old one on a deadline.
Revoke one credential now, keeping the row.
Categories and states with counts, and how many need attention.
Every integration, filtered and faceted in PostgreSQL.
One integration with its configuration; secrets come back redacted.
Turn an integration on or off; refused while settings are missing.
Verify the configuration, saying it did not contact the provider.
What can be exported, the ceilings that apply, and where mine stand.
My exports, newest first, filtered and faceted in PostgreSQL.
How many rows a query has, and whether it streams or must be queued.
Accept an export and start producing it off the request.
One export with its log lines; DELETE drops the file and keeps the record.
A signed URL for the finished file, so the bytes bypass this worker.
Queue a new export from an existing one's stored query.
What can be imported into, what each field accepts, and the limits.
My imports, newest first, filtered and faceted in PostgreSQL.
Accept a CSV, read it, and propose a column mapping.
One import with its preview; DELETE discards a draft and its staged file.
Set which column is which field, and validate every row.
Write the valid rows in one transaction, off the request.
The row-level error report as a CSV, to fix in the spreadsheet.
Is anything wrong with this account, in one glance.
Every sign-in on this account, with the current one marked.
Trust a device, or DELETE to sign it out — enforced on its next request.
Sign out everywhere else, keeping this session.
Recent sign-ins, successes and failures, filtered in PostgreSQL.
What the platform has noticed about this account.
Mark one security event as dealt with, or as not.
Every bookmark, in the order this person arranged them.
Bookmark something addressable, checked against the platform's registry.
Unstar one thing.
Put the bookmarks in the order somebody dragged them into.
What this person has looked at lately, most recent first.
Record a visit, upserted and trimmed.
Forget the trail. All of it or none.
